title: Climbing Stairs
interviewTips: Clarify if n can be 0 and whether order matters: here 1+2 and 2+1 count as distinct, giving f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2).
Trade-off to discuss: brute-force recursion is O(2^n), memoization fixes it to O(n) with O(n) stack+cache, bottom-up iterative achieves O(1) space and avoids recursion depth.
Edge cases to test: n=1, n=2, n=3, n=45 (max constraint fits 32-bit signed int); mention overflow to 64-bit if constraints grew.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Recursion
approaches.intuition: From step n you must have come from n-1 with a 1-step or from n-2 with a 2-step. So total ways is sum of ways to reach those two previous steps. Recursively explore both choices.
approaches.theory: Defines recurrence f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2) with base f(1)=1, f(2)=2. Recursion builds a binary decision tree where each node branches to n-1 and n-2. Correct by exhaustive enumeration of all 1/2 sequences, but overlapping subproblems are recomputed exponentially many times.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each call spawns two calls, recursion tree has ~2^n nodes. For n=45 this TLEs.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Maximum recursion depth is n due to repeated n-1 path.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Top-Down DP with Memoization
approaches.intuition: Brute force recomputes the same f(k) many times. Cache result of each k after first computation so each state is solved once.
approaches.theory: Memoized DFS preserves recurrence f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2) but memo array guarantees each i in [1..n] is expanded at most once. This converts exponential tree into linear DAG traversal. Correctness follows from optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems.

timeComplexity.explanation: n distinct states, each computed once with O(1) work combining two cached values.

spaceComplexity.explanation: O(n) memo array plus O(n) recursion stack depth.

edgeCases: n=45 easily passes, recursion depth 45 is safe
Repeated calls reuse cache within single query

approaches.name: Approach 3: Bottom-Up DP Tabulation
approaches.intuition: Compute answers from small to large: ways to reach step i only depends on previous two steps, so fill table iteratively.
approaches.theory: Define dp[1]=1, dp[2]=2, dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2] for i>=3. By induction dp[i] equals number of distinct sequences to reach i. Iterative order guarantees dependencies are already solved. This is Fibonacci shifted: answer is Fib(n+1).

timeComplexity.explanation: Single linear pass from 3 to n with O(1) transition.

spaceComplexity.explanation: dp array of size n+1 stores all subanswers.

approaches.name: Approach 4: Space-Optimized Iterative Fibonacci
approaches.intuition: Only the last two values are needed to compute the next. Keep two rolling variables instead of full array.
approaches.theory: Since dp[i] depends only on dp[i-1] and dp[i-2], we maintain a= f(i-2), b=f(i-1) and iterate c=a+b. Invariant after each iteration: b = f(current). This is O(n) time Fibonacci iteration with constant memory, optimal for interview constraints. Can be extended to O(log n) via matrix exponentiation if needed.

timeComplexity.explanation: n-2 iterations, each O(1). Optimal for linear DP; O(log n) matrix method possible but unnecessary for n<=45.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two integer variables regardless of n, no recursion or array.

edgeCases: Large n would need long/BigInteger to avoid overflow
